theory.intro: The **probability** that a normally distributed score falls in an interval is the **area** under the bell curve over that interval. The whole area is $1$, and the empirical rule supplies approximate areas at whole numbers of standard deviations from the mean. All numerical questions in this skill use the empirical rule, rather than normal distribution table values; their calculated probabilities and expected frequencies are estimates.
facts: The total area under a normal curve is $1$, because every score lies somewhere under it.
The empirical rule gives $P(\mu-\sigma < X < \mu+\sigma) \approx 0.68$, $P(\mu-2\sigma < X < \mu+2\sigma) \approx 0.95$ and $P(\mu-3\sigma < X < \mu+3\sigma) \approx 0.997$.
$P(X < \mu) = 0.5$ and $P(X > \mu) = 0.5$, because the curve is symmetrical about the mean.
Half of each band lies on each side of the mean, so the empirical-rule estimates are $P(\mu < X < \mu+\sigma) \approx 0.34$ and $P(\mu < X < \mu+2\sigma) \approx 0.475$.
Each tail is half of what is left over, so the empirical-rule estimate is $P(X > \mu+2\sigma) \approx (1-0.95)\div 2 = 0.025$.
An **expected frequency** is $f = np$: multiply the number of items $n$ by the probability $p$, then round to a whole number.
steps: Write each boundary as a number of standard deviations from the mean
Shade the required region on a normal curve
Add the empirical-rule areas inside the shaded region
Multiply the probability by $n$ for an expected frequency

foundation.question_text:
A dataset is normally distributed with a mean of $60$ and a standard deviation of $5$.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen score lies between $50$ and $70$.

A dataset is normally distributed with a mean of $88$ and a standard deviation of $7$.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen score is greater than $102$.

A dataset is normally distributed with a mean of $45$ and a standard deviation of $3$.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen score is less than $36$.

A dataset is normally distributed with a mean of $120$ and a standard deviation of $8$.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen score is less than $128$.

A dataset is normally distributed with a mean of $250$ and a standard deviation of $20$.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen score is greater than $210$.

A dataset is normally distributed with a mean of $32$ and a standard deviation of $4$.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen score lies between $36$ and $40$.

A dataset is normally distributed with a mean of $500$ and a standard deviation of $30$.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen score lies between $410$ and $440$.

A dataset is normally distributed with a mean of $15$ and a standard deviation of $2$.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen score lies between $11$ and $17$.

A dataset is normally distributed with a mean of $70$ and a standard deviation of $6$.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen score lies between $52$ and $88$.

development.question_text: The masses of $800$ apples in a delivery are normally distributed with a mean of $150$ g and a standard deviation of $10$ g. How many apples are expected to have a mass greater than $170$ g?

A farmer harvests $1200$ pumpkins whose masses are normally distributed with a mean of $6.2$ kg and a standard deviation of $0.9$ kg.
How many pumpkins are expected to have a mass between $5.3$ kg and $7.1$ kg?

A crate holds $2000$ batteries whose lifetimes are normally distributed with a mean of $480$ hours and a standard deviation of $25$ hours.
How many batteries are expected to last less than $430$ hours?

The daily maximum temperature in a town is normally distributed with a mean of $24.0^{\circ}$C and a standard deviation of $3.0^{\circ}$C. Find the probability that a day's maximum temperature is between $18.0^{\circ}$C and $33.0^{\circ}$C.

The times taken by athletes to run $400$ m are normally distributed with a mean of $52$ seconds and a standard deviation of $2$ seconds.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen athlete runs the race in less than $50$ seconds.

A hardware store stocks $300$ timber battens whose lengths are normally distributed with a mean of $22$ cm and a standard deviation of $2$ cm.
How many battens are expected to be longer than $20$ cm?

A machine pours drinks whose volumes are normally distributed with a mean of $250$ mL and a standard deviation of $4$ mL.
One cup contains $262$ mL.
Use the empirical rule to decide whether this volume is unusual, supporting your answer with a probability.

The diameters of ball bearings are normally distributed with a mean of $12.0$ mm and a standard deviation of $0.2$ mm.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen bearing has a diameter between $11.6$ mm and $11.8$ mm.

mastery.question_text:
A factory tests $3500$ electronic components whose working lives are normally distributed with a mean of $1200$ hours and a standard deviation of $90$ hours.
How many components are expected to last between $1020$ hours and $1290$ hours? Round to the nearest whole component.

A dataset is normally distributed with a mean of $76$ and a standard deviation of $8$.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen score lies between $52$ and $92$.

The masses of newborn lambs are normally distributed with a mean of $4.5$ kg and a standard deviation of $0.35$ kg.
One lamb weighs $3.45$ kg.
Use the empirical rule to decide whether this mass is unusual, supporting your answer with a probability.

A production line fills $600$ packets whose masses are normally distributed with a mean of $205$ g and a standard deviation of $5$ g. A packet is underweight if its mass is below $195$ g. How many of the $600$ packets are expected to be underweight?
